message.content: I have strong evidence. Let me compute the key changes.

**Norfolk Southern Corp. (CIK 702165) — revenue and traffic-volume trend**

**Revenue (railway operating revenues, USD, fiscal years ended Dec. 31):** Revenue rose from $11.46bn in 2018 to $12.75bn in 2022, dipped to $12.16bn in 2023, and was essentially flat at $12.12bn in 2024. The 2024 figure was down only $33m (about −0.3%) versus 2023, while 2023 was down $589m (about −4.9%) versus 2022. (Fact IDs 859649, 859670, 859688, 859702, 859715, 859727, 859736; the 2022–2024 values come from the FY2024 10-K, accession 0000702165-25-000008, filed 2025-02-10.)

**Traffic volumes (units in thousands, from the FY2024 10-K, Item 7 tables):**
- Total units: 6,834.5 (2022) → 6,744.4 (2023, −1%) → 7,056.8 (2024, +5%).
- Merchandise: 2,236.8 → 2,244.9 (flat) → 2,264.3 (+1%).
- Intermodal: 3,913.1 → 3,822.4 (−2%) → 4,107.7 (+7%); domestic 2,573.6 → 2,371.6 (−8%) → 2,500.0 (+5%); international 1,339.5 → 1,450.8 (+8%) → 1,607.7 (+11%).
- Coal: 684.6 → 677.1 (−1%) → 684.8 (+1%); coal tonnage fell in 2023 (utility tons 35,705 → 30,419, −15%) and utility tons fell a further 3% in 2024 to 29,577.
- Revenue ton miles (billions): 164 (2020), 178 (2021), 179 (2022), 176 (2023), 178 (2024) — broadly flat over 2021–2024.

**Interpretation:** The two series diverged. Volumes were roughly flat-to-down in 2023 and rebounded about 5% in 2024, yet revenue fell in both years. Management attributes this to lower average revenue per unit — lower fuel surcharge revenue (fuel surcharge revenue fell from $1.6bn in 2022 to $1.2bn in 2023 and $962m in 2024), reduced intermodal storage revenue, and pricing/mix effects — rather than to volume. Total revenue per unit declined from $1,865 (2022) to $1,802 (2023) to $1,718 (2024). In 2024, volume contributed +$64m (merchandise), +$231m (intermodal) and +$19m (coal) to revenue, but these gains were more than offset by fuel surcharge declines (−$131m, −$101m, −$29m) and rate/mix effects. (Chunks 702165/nsc-20241231:94400, :96000, :97600, :104000.)

**Overall trend:** Over 2022–2024, revenue trended modestly downward (about −4.9% cumulative) while total traffic units were roughly flat to slightly up (about +3.3% cumulative), so the revenue decline reflects price/fuel-surcharge and mix compression rather than weaker volumes. Management stated it expects 2025 revenue to increase on higher volumes (forward-looking statement, not a realized result).

*Note:* These are railway operating revenues and reported (GAAP) units; the 2023 operating ratio of 76.5% includes the Ohio derailment ("the Incident") costs, and adjusted figures are separate non-GAAP measures not used here.

**Revenue (railway operating revenues, USD, fiscal years ended Dec. 31):** Revenue rose from $11.46bn in 2018 to $12.75bn in 2022, dipped to $12.16bn in 2023, and was essentially flat at $12.12bn in 2024. The 2024 figure was down only $33m (about −0.3%) versus 2023, while 2023 was down $589m (about −4.9%) versus 2022. (Fact IDs 859649, 859670, 859688, 859702, 859715, 859727, 859736; the 2022–2024 values come from the FY2024 10-K, accession 0000702165-25-000008, filed 2025-02-10.)

**Traffic volumes (units in thousands, from the FY2024 10-K, Item 7 tables):**
- Total units: 6,834.5 (2022) → 6,744.4 (2023, −1%) → 7,056.8 (2024, +5%).
- Merchandise: 2,236.8 → 2,244.9 (flat) → 2,264.3 (+1%).
- Intermodal: 3,913.1 → 3,822.4 (−2%) → 4,107.7 (+7%); domestic 2,573.6 → 2,371.6 (−8%) → 2,500.0 (+5%); international 1,339.5 → 1,450.8 (+8%) → 1,607.7 (+11%).
- Coal: 684.6 → 677.1 (−1%) → 684.8 (+1%); coal tonnage fell in 2023 (utility tons 35,705 → 30,419, −15%) and utility tons fell a further 3% in 2024 to 29,577.
- Revenue ton miles (billions): 164 (2020), 178 (2021), 179 (2022), 176 (2023), 178 (2024) — broadly flat over 2021–2024.

**Interpretation:** The two series diverged. Volumes were roughly flat-to-down in 2023 and rebounded about 5% in 2024, yet revenue fell in both years. Management attributes this to lower average revenue per unit — lower fuel surcharge revenue (fuel surcharge revenue fell from $1.6bn in 2022 to $1.2bn in 2023 and $962m in 2024), reduced intermodal storage revenue, and pricing/mix effects — rather than to volume. Total revenue per unit declined from $1,865 (2022) to $1,802 (2023) to $1,718 (2024). In 2024, volume contributed +$64m (merchandise), +$231m (intermodal) and +$19m (coal) to revenue, but these gains were more than offset by fuel surcharge declines (−$131m, −$101m, −$29m) and rate/mix effects. (Chunks 702165/nsc-20241231:94400, :96000, :97600, :104000.)

**Overall trend:** Over 2022–2024, revenue trended modestly downward (about −4.9% cumulative) while total traffic units were roughly flat to slightly up (about +3.3% cumulative), so the revenue decline reflects price/fuel-surcharge and mix compression rather than weaker volumes. Management stated it expects 2025 revenue to increase on higher volumes (forward-looking statement, not a realized result).

*Note:* These are railway operating revenues and reported (GAAP) units; the 2023 operating ratio of 76.5% includes the Ohio derailment ("the Incident") costs, and adjusted figures are separate non-GAAP measures not used here.
